state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: What if we consider the relationship between time and distance in a different way? How might the movement of an object affect the shape of the graph?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess the graph shows how far Fido is from home, so when it goes down, it means he’s getting closer to home, right? But if he’s not moving, like when he’s asleep, wouldn’t the line just stay flat? I’m still a bit confused about how to tell the difference between resting and moving on the graph.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me ask you this: how can we distinguish between rest and movement on a distance-time graph based on the slope of the line?

score.justification_pass1: While the teacher's questions are mathematically accurate and the student does show improvement by Turn 2 (correctly identifying that flat=rest and slope=movement), the teacher's generic questioning approach doesn't directly address the specific misconception, and the final question essentially asks the student to state the rule rather than reason through it.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking without directly providing the answer, helping them discover the relationship between slope and movement on distance-time graphs through their own reasoning.
